reference_sql:
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', i.invoice_date) AS DATE) AS month_start, s.currency, SUM(i.amount_local / 12) AS renewal_mrr
FROM invoices i
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = i.subscription_id
WHERE s.billing_period = 'annual'
  AND i.invoice_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  AND month(i.invoice_date) = month(s.start_date)
  AND day(i.invoice_date) = day(s.start_date)
GROUP BY CAST(date_trunc('month', i.invoice_date) AS DATE), s.currency

WITH renewals AS (
  -- one row per annual invoice on a start day or an anniversary in 2025
  SELECT i.invoice_date, s.currency, i.amount_local / 12 AS mrr_local
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = i.subscription_id
  WHERE s.billing_period = 'annual'
    AND i.invoice_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
    AND month(i.invoice_date) = month(s.start_date)
    AND day(i.invoice_date) = day(s.start_date)
)
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', invoice_date) AS DATE) AS month_start, currency, SUM(mrr_local) AS renewal_mrr
FROM renewals
GROUP BY CAST(date_trunc('month', invoice_date) AS DATE), currency

other_way.tradeoff: Turning each invoice into a month's MRR in a CTE first makes the twelfth hard to forget, at the cost of one more step.
